title: GPU-Accelerated Monte Carlo Option Pricing
tech: Python · NumPy · Numba CUDA · PyTorch · Matplotlib · pandas
description: Built a quantitative-finance benchmark that prices European options by Monte Carlo simulation on both CPU and GPU, validates the results against the analytical Black-Scholes formula, and measures how the GPU speedup grows with problem size.
bullets: Wrote a custom [[[Numba CUDA]]] kernel that prices one option path per GPU thread, generalized by a [[grid-stride loop]]{A pattern where each thread strides across multiple work items, so the same kernel runs efficiently whether there are 10K or 10M paths — the launch is sized for the hardware, not the data.} so the same kernel scales from 10K to 10M paths

Cut memory contention with a block-level [[shared-memory reduction]]{Each block sums its threads' payoffs in fast on-chip memory using an O(log n) tree, then one thread does a single atomicAdd to a global total — avoiding millions of threads serializing on one counter.}, copying back only two scalars to minimize [[[PCIe]]] transfer

Generated random numbers on-device with a per-thread [[xoroshiro128+]]{A counter-based RNG where each GPU thread owns an independent sub-stream keyed by its global id, avoiding the correlated draws and race conditions you'd get from sharing one generator across threads.} stream, keeping the entire simulation on the GPU

Validated correctness against the closed-form [[[Black-Scholes]]] price and benchmarked CPU vs GPU across problem sizes, showing speedup grow with path count at the expected [[1/√N]]{Monte Carlo error shrinks proportionally to one over the square root of the number of paths — so halving the error requires 4× the simulations, which is exactly why the workload is compute-hungry and ideal for GPUs.} convergence rate

title: Influence Proxy Dashboard
tech: Next.js · FastAPI · PyTorch · HuggingFace · PEFT · Modal · Supabase
description: Built a full-stack research tool that lets AI safety researchers fine-tune language models and see exactly which training examples shaped the model's behavior — turning fine-tuning from a black box into an auditable process.
bullets: Computed [[influence scores]]{A measure of how much a specific training example shaped a model's prediction on a given input — used here to make fine-tuning auditable instead of a black box.} live during training using [[gradient dot products]]{Comparing the gradient direction of a training example to the gradient of a test prediction; a high dot product means that example likely influenced the prediction.}, with no checkpoint storage required
Ran serverless A100 GPU jobs on [[[Modal]]] with async status updates streamed to the frontend in real time
Visualized per-example influence as animated heatmaps and ranked leaderboards for intuitive data auditing
Designed a full job pipeline from data upload through fine-tuning to influence score delivery via [[[Supabase Realtime]]]

title: Covid-19 Vaccine Stance Classification
tech: Python · PyTorch · Hugging Face · FLAN-T5 · LoRA · bitsandbytes · scikit-learn
description: Built a stance classification system to label tweets as in-favor, against, or neutral-or-unclear toward COVID-19 vaccination under tight data and GPU constraints.
bullets: Fine-tuned [[[FLAN-T5]]] using [[[LoRA]]] adapters, training on limited resources

Designed a [[curriculum learning]]{Training the model on easier examples first and gradually introducing harder ones, rather than feeding it randomly-ordered data from the start — used here to stabilize 3-way classification.} strategy to stabilize 3-way stance classification

Mitigated failure modes including [[neutral collapse]]{When a classifier defaults to predicting the majority/neutral class too often, especially under class imbalance, rather than correctly distinguishing genuine stance.}, sarcasm, and more
Achieved improved macro-F1 and neutral recall compared to zero-shot and standard fine-tuning baselines
